Rogue Legacy 2 is a extremely well-made and well-polished good game. It's not a [i]fantastic[/i] game - it doesn't amaze or thrill - but it does what it's trying to do extremely competently. 

The house upgrade system provides the progression, new game+ provides the game length, the classes provide the gameplay variety, and the room, enemy, and boss design tie it all together to make a satisfying game to play. It's got secrets, side-challenges, a story and lore, alternate modes, accessibility options, pretty much anything you could ask for.

I likely would have enjoyed it a bit more if it were a 50-hour game instead, but even when it had become a bit rote it was still pleasant to play, and there was still room to grow and get better.

Good game.

Wanted to wrire a review full of glazing and explaining why i like it, but then realised that nobody really cares. If you need it, know that it's a great game you'll probably enjoy playing, no matter who you are and what games you like.

RL2 refines every aspect of an already fantastic roguelite, especially with its diverse weapons and genuinely distinct playable classes

Like Dead Cells, but much worse.

Three things and it might be personal taste or just bad design. I'll let you decide.

1. The character is ginormous and looks clumsy when they move and feels clumsy when they play.
2. Enemies shoot you from offscreen. A lot. Which that's never good game design imo.
3. This is much more of a parkour game than something like Dead Cells. It has similar opponents and similar controls and similar movement, but it comes at you with the platforming as hard as it comes at you with the opponents and when you combine this with issue number 1 it just doesn't work well.

I wouldn't recommend it at any price because there are other options which are much better.
It is ultra grindy cookie clicker where you must die infinite times to upgrade your character. I don't like it.

I really wanted to like this as a huge fan of the first game, but every second of this game is agony. In as nice a way as I can put it: it feels like a fan project more than anything. Like someone's outside perspective on the game and what it should be, instead of ANYTHING the original game had going for it. gg go next I guess.

No, getting hit constantly by offscreen enemies should not be the norm.
No, putting the player in a closet with traps and a projectile spamming boss that floats at you is not okay.
No, adding a second boss to the closet does not make it better.
No, a player should not die in three hits despite farming the whole map every run.
No, making five of the eight bosses randomly overlay several projectile attacks at a time is not game design. 
No, adding more sets of projectiles to the boss won't fix that.
No, the boss minions that home in on the player should not be invincible for 30 seconds during his other attacks.
No, the correct response to overwhelming negative feedback on a new mode isn't to suggest players enable cheats for it.

No, the devs shouldn't be proud of any of this.
No, absolutely not.
